summary: Discovery focused on requirements for a fully on-prem, air-gapped Redwood Private deployment for regulated pharma workloads. Primary concerns: offline model updates, hardware constraints (older generation GPUs), KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and validation timeline. AE+SE to provide SOC2 pack, sizing, and schedule bench-marking in customer lab.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Eli Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CISO, Alder Biotech), Tom Reyes (Platform Eng), Nina Flores (AI/ML Eng), Rajiv Menon (IT Ops)
Recording/platform: Zoom / Fireflies

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro — I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on this account, and Eli is our solutions engineer. How are you all?

[00:16] Maya (CISO): Good, thanks. Busy but ready.

[00:22] Eli (Redwood SE): Hi folks, hello. we'll cover on-prem private, air-gapped specifics, tradeoffs vs hosted/dedicated, and then dive into their update and patch workflow. Apologies in advance if my mic is a little off.

[00:34] Tom (Platform): No problem. To set context — Alder is in regulated pharma discovery; anything with patient-derived sequences or IP needs to remain on-prem and in our air-gapped lab. We're evaluating options: keep everything in-house, or use vendors who can do a fully offline deployment.

[00:48] Samira: Great. Can we go through a couple of qualification items quickly? Timeline, success criteria, and who signs off on security?

[00:56] Maya: Timeline — we'd like a pilot within Q4, production in Q1. Success criteria: no external egress from inference hosts, ability to update models without internet (air-gap update process), integration with our HSM for keys, and full audit trail for all inference requests. Security approver: that's me and our compliance officer (I'll loop them in).

[01:18] Samira: Perfect. Eli, do you want to take the technical constraints?

[01:22] Eli: Sure. A few top-level notes: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages; we've done fully air-gapped installs with customers before, but specifics vary — e.g. how you want to do model updates: via signed bundles on physical media, or scheduled import through an ephemeral jumpbox. Also, hardware: we can run on A100 or H100 series, plus NVMe caching for large models. But we need to size for your concurrency and latency SLOs.

[01:45] Rajiv (IT Ops): Quick flag — our current GPU fleet is a mix, mostly A100-40GB and a couple of older A100-v1 nodes; we don't have H100s available in the air-gapped lab and procurement lead times are long. Can Redwood run on v1 A100s with quantized models?

[02:02] Eli: Yes, we can. We'll recommend quantization and kernel selection tuned for older GPUs. Throughput will be lower, but it's often an acceptable trade. We'll also look at model variants small enough to meet latency SLOs.

[02:15] Nina (ML): What about model size? We're looking to run an LLM for structured output and reranking. We're assuming off-the-shelf open models, maybe some customer-finetuned weights. We need to understand memory KV cache behavior for longer sequences.

[02:29] Eli: Good question. Redwood's runtime handles KV cache and continuous batching; for long sequences you'll want larger GPU memory or sharded KV across nodes. In air-gapped setups we sometimes recommend prefix caching on NVMe to avoid blowing GPU memory. There's a performance tradeoff but it keeps latency stable.

[02:46] Tom: On compliance — we need all telemetry off by default. No usage telemetry can leave the air-gapped environment. Is that possible?

[02:53] Samira: Absolutely. Our Private package can run with telemetry disabled. The control plane can be hosted or you can run our private control plane; in fully air-gapped scenarios we provide a customer-managed control plane image. We'll also support local logging only.

[03:08] Maya: How do you do key management? We need to use our HSM; keys must never be exportable.

[03:13] Eli: We integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 and can be configured to use the HSM for signing model bundles and for encrypting keys at rest. For air-gapped model updates we produce signed artifacts that your on-prem updater verifies using the HSM.

[03:28] Rajiv: So the update flow would be — Redwood builds signed model bundle, we get the bundle on a USB or secure courier, and then our internal tool verifies signature against the HSM and installs?

[03:36] Eli: Exactly. That is one pattern. Another is an offline jumpbox: you transfer the signed bundle to the jumpbox, run the import, and the jumpbox has no external network. Both are common.

[03:46] Nina: Any support for model quantization tooling offline? We can't send weights to Redwood for quantization.

[03:52] Eli: We have two options: we can provide an approved quantization toolkit and scripts you can run in your air-gap to produce quantized artifacts; or we can run the process on-prem as a professional service engagement if you want us on-site for the first run. We often ship container images with the tooling that run entirely offline.

[04:10] Maya: One more: audit logs. We need immutable logs for each inference request — timestamps, model version, requesting service identity — for at least seven years. Can Redwood's Private provide that?

[04:20] Eli: Yes, we log request-level metadata locally and we can configure log retention and write-once encryption policies. For regulatory retention, we'd recommend exporting to your long-term WORM storage — we can write to an on-prem S3-compatible WORM store.

[04:34] Tom: Are those logs human-readable or compressed? Our compliance team wants readable indexes for audits.

[04:40] Eli: They are JSON lines by default; we can include indexing metadata. We also have a small indexer tool in the Private package that runs locally for search.

[04:50] Samira: I want to touch on fallback modes briefly — suppose you want the safety of Redwood Hosted as a fallback. For air-gapped regulated workloads that's often not allowed, but for non-sensitive paths some customers use dedicated hosted failover. Is failover a requirement?

[05:05] Maya: Not allowed for regulated data — no external fallback. For non-sensitive models maybe. But for this initial scope, no external egress at all.

[05:14] Samira: Understood. We'll treat this as fully air-gapped.

[05:18] Rajiv: Networking — our environment is strictly segmented. The inference nodes are behind a firewall with only internal routing. Do you require any outbound connectivity for license checks or heartbeats?

[05:29] Eli: For air-gapped installs we can run without outbound license checks; we issue time-bound license bundles that you validate locally. That said, some customers choose periodic online check-ins via a secure, customer-controlled proxy for license renewal; but that's optional.

[05:44] Nina: Performance: we hypothesize needing ~50 concurrent requests at 200ms p95 for reranking requests. Will A100-v1 handle that?

[05:54] Eli: We'll need to model that — 50 concurrent with 200ms p95 is aggressive on older A100s unless model is small or quantized heavily. We'll run a benchmark plan to give empirical numbers. For some customers we tune batching and micro-batching to meet p95.

[06:10] Tom: Cost question — since procurement is slow, we want to maximize existing hardware. Is there a licensing model that doesn't charge per GPU? We prefer a flat license for Private plus seats/support.

[06:20] Samira: We support a few licensing models: flat platform fee + support, or per-GPU license, or committed capacity for Dedicated equivalents. For enterprise Private deals we typically do platform + support and then add professional services for deployment and bench. We'll send pricing options.

[06:33] Maya: Encryption at rest — do you support customer KMS integration with rotation policies?

[06:38] Eli: Yes, we integrate with HSM/KMS and support automatic rotation policies defined by you. Keys used to encrypt model artifacts are stored only in the HSM.

[06:46] Rajiv: About physical security — our auditors require signed chain-of-custody for any physical media. Does Redwood assist with generating the signed bundle and chain-of-custody manifest?

[06:55] Eli: We can generate a signed manifest and include a signature that your HSM can verify. Chain-of-custody per se is more of a logistics process, but we can provide the signed artifacts and recommended manifests for your operations team.

[07:08] Nina: For model updates, how do you handle dependency on third-party libs? Many of our models depend on specific custom ops.

[07:15] Eli: In Private deployments we allow you to install custom libraries; we typically containerize the runtime so you control the base image. For custom ops, we recommend packaging them into your runtime image and we'll validate compatibility.

[07:28] Samira: Quick question on stakeholders — who signs off on procurement and security? Maya for security, Tom for platform procurement, and Rajiv for ops. We'll need to engage Alder's procurement early.

[07:38] Maya: Correct. Also, our legal team needs to see data processing addendum and a signed NDA before we exchange sample data.

[07:46] Samira: We will share NDA and SOC2/ISO docs after this call.

[07:50] [08:00–40 min] (longer technical dive, paraphrased highlights)
- Eli walked through an offline update diagram (mis-named slide 'privy update flow' in notes) showing signed bundles -> courier -> jumpbox -> HSM verification -> deployment.
- Discussed quantization options: 8-bit quant / PTQ vs QAT considerations; Redwood recommends PTQ plus small eval set for check.
- Bench plan: 2 hours in Alder lab, run 3 model sizes, measure p95 and cost per token; Eli to provision benchmark harness and scripts.
- Discussed telemetry off by default, local-only logs, and WORM export.

[36:00] Tom: For the bench session, do you need any connectivity from our network to Redwood?

[36:10] Eli: No, the harness can run entirely locally. We'll ship a docker tar or a signed VM image that runs locally and outputs results CSVs.

[36:22] Maya: Can we get sample audit logs so our auditors can see format?

[36:26] Samira: Yes, we'll attach sample logs and the schema in the docs pack.

[36:34] Rajiv: About support — what is the on-call model? If a node goes down in the air-gapped lab at 2am, how quickly can Redwood respond?

[36:42] Samira: We offer 24/7 enterprise support as an add-on with guaranteed SLA windows. For air-gapped installs we often include runbook training and optionally an on-site support retainer. We'll include options in the proposal.

[36:58] Nina: Any known limitations with long-sequence inference and older GPUs? We saw tokenization + KV cache spikes in past tests.

[37:06] Eli: Older GPUs may see GC-like memory pressure for long sequences; we mitigate via NVMe prefix caching and batching limits. We'll capture these in the bench plan.

[37:18] Maya: Compliance question — does Redwood provide evidence of SOC2 controls that cover your deployment process for customer-run Private installs?

[37:26] Samira: We will share our SOC2 report and a customer-specific controls mapping that shows which controls remain with the customer for on-prem installs.

[37:36] Tom: What's the expected installation timeline once contract signed? We need a rough project plan for procurement.

[37:43] Eli: Typical on-prem air-gapped deployments are 4–8 weeks including hardware validation, image signing, and initial install. If you want on-site support it may add a week for scheduling. We'll produce a draft timeline in the proposal.

[37:56] Maya: License audit — do you require runtime phone-home for license reporting? We said no earlier but just confirming.

[38:03] Eli: No phone-home required for air-gapped. Time-bound license bundles are common; renewal requires a new signed bundle delivered through your process.

[38:12] Samira: To summarize action items and next steps — I'll send SOC2/ISO + NDA, Eli will draft bench plan and hardware sizing, Tom will share network diagram and procurement calendar, Nina will share sample prompts/workload, and we'll schedule the bench in your lab. Anything else?

[38:28] Maya: Please include documentation on chain-of-custody for physical media.

[38:34] Samira: Yes. We'll include an example manifest and recommended processes.

[38:40] Rajiv: Also include the quantization toolkit and the offline container images.

[38:45] Eli: We'll provide a signed container image and quant toolkit scripts that run offline.

[38:50] Samira: Great. Timeline recap: docs by 2025-08-21, bench plan by 2025-08-22, customer to return diagrams and prompts by 2025-08-23, bench week TBD but aiming late September.

[39:05] Maya: Sounds good. We'll review and follow up.

[39:10] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links: SOC2 doc, on-prem playbook, and the bench scheduling poll.

[39:18] (small crosstalk)

[39:25] Meeting end / off-record chatter

Notes / links mentioned: SOC2 pack (link placeholder), On-prem deployment guide (link placeholder), Bench harness repo (link placeholder).

End of transcript.
